gary_2026_09_18_founders_makers_coworkin.summary: Gary's Guide: A full day of heads-down work at No More, with other people who are actually building things. No talks. No panels. No pitch round. Just a good room, good coffee, & everyone finally getting through the thing they have been putting off all month. Why this space works No More is genuinely built for working, which is rarer in this city than it should be. Outlets everywhere, so nobody is rationing battery by 2 PM Fast wifi that holds up with a room full of laptops Music stays low, so you can take a call without walking outside Long communal tables & a full counter, room to actually spread out Coffee & snacks all day without leaving your seat Who it is for Founders, researchers, designers, creatives, engineers, writers, & anyone with a side project they keep meaning to ship. If you build things, you belong here. How the day runs 9:00 AM, doors open, coffee & quick introductions 9:30 AM to 5:00 PM, open work, break whenever you need to 5:00 PM, mocktails, & we find out what everyone actually got done Food & coffee Nothing structured. The cafe has coffee & snacks all day, & the East Village is full of options if you want a proper meal. The company Honestly the main reason to come. A room where everyone is working on something they care about changes how your own day goes. Quiet focus while the work is happening, real conversation over mocktails at the end. Come for the whole day or drop in for a few hours. Both are fine. Bring your laptop, your headphones, & real work. Space is limited, so please only register if you actually plan to show up. Hosted by Ishaan from TechBrig.

gary_2026_09_19_trust_in_the_hiring_funn.title: Trust In The Hiring Funnel Hackathon
gary_2026_09_19_trust_in_the_hiring_funn.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_19_trust_in_the_hiring_funn.summary: Gary's Guide: Event Description Generative AI broke hiring on both sides at once. Recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Come spend a day building something that fixes it - with the founders, engineers, & TA practitioners who live this problem every week. This is a full-day, in-person hackathon co-hosted by localhost:nyc, Integral Recruiting (IRD), & NYU - where builders team up with real talent-acquisition operators to ship working tools against a single, focused challenge. The Challenge: Trust in the Hiring Funnel Hiring has a trust crisis on both sides of the funnel - recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Talent acquisition runs on a basic assumption: that the person applying is who they say they are, & that the company reaching out is who it says it is. Generative AI has broken both halves of that assumption at once. Your job for the day is to rebuild it. You can attack either side of the funnel - or the seam between them. Side A - Trust coming in: the applicant flood. A role that used to draw 30 applicants now draws 500, & a growing share aren't real, aren't qualified, or are gaming the system. Candidates embed hidden prompt-injection text to manipulate the AI tools that screen resumes. And increasingly, applicants appear qualified but look strikingly alike - the same phrasing, the same structure, the same accomplishments - a tell that everyone is leaning on the same AI tools to write their applications. Recruiters are drowning, & the tools meant to help have no clear winner yet. The challenge: reliably separate real, qualified humans from AI-inflated noise - without punishing legitimate candidates who simply used AI to polish their resume. Questions worth chasing: What signals - behavioral, identity, provenance - actually distinguish a real applicant from a manufactured one? When applications converge on the same AI-generated look, how do you tell genuine signal from sameness? How do you detect a manipulated or machine-generated application without false-flagging honest people? How do you surface the candidates who deserve attention fast, inside an existing recruiting workflow rather than replacing it? Side B - Trust going out: impersonation & candidate scams. Bad actors register look-alike domains to send fake offer letters, run deepfake recruiter calls, & scam job seekers out of money & data. Employers have almost no way to detect it or warn candidates. The challenge: make it harder to impersonate a real employer, & easier for a candidate to verify that an offer or a recruiter is genuine. Questions worth chasing: How would a candidate confirm that an offer or outreach is legitimately from the company? Can impersonating domains be detected & flagged early? What does a lightweight "trust signal" look like on a careers page or an offer letter? What a strong build looks like. A working tool that raises trust in the funnel & fits the way hiring actually happens - a triage or screening layer that plugs into an existing applicant tracking system rather than replacing it, or a candidate/employer verification tool that makes impersonation harder to pull off & easier to catch. We care more about a real, demonstrable solution to a narrow slice of the problem than a broad concept that doesn't run. You don't need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete here - that's the point of a single, focused theme. Engineers & builders can go straight at the detection, identity, & verification problems. HR-technology practitioners will be in the room to keep your build grounded in how hiring actually works, & to pressure-test whether a recruiter would trust what you've made. What to Expect A full day of building - 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM, hard stop Small teams (or solo if you insist) working in one shared room TA practitioners from the SAI community in the room to keep your build grounded in how hiring really works A panel of expert judges: HR-tech founders, operators, & system admins who know these problems cold End-of-day demos to judges, investors, & real TA leaders The strongest teams get connected to investors - and, over time, to real customers Prizes Winners walk away with build-tool & platform credits, expert consulting sessions, & investor time. Everyone in the room gets connections that outlast the day - this is a room full of builders & buyers. Judges Tiffany Jin: Eqo. Building in the employee-referral & hiring space; brings a founder's eye for what actually ships. Steven Grover: Partnerspring. Operator & builder in the HR-tech ecosystem. Shane Papp: Ex-iCIMS. Deep insider knowledge of the ATS world these tools have to live inside. Adam Treitler: Related Industries. HR-tech operator with a practitioner's view of the funnel. Shiv Jethi - Engineer at SpaceX. Olivia Iarmak - Meta Reality Labs. AI quality & operations leader; researcher. Brings a practitioner's lens to trustworthy AI. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Prince Rumi - Excelsior Edge Ventures, Partner | AI Researcher Rami Abouemira, formerly People Ops at Square & VMware, now building the future of work with All Good HR & Founders Foundry. Ishaan Das (TechBrig) - Leads AI transformation & product design for several recruiting firms & recruiting SaaS like SquarePeg. More judges to be announced - investors & TA buyers joining the panel. Who Should Attend Engineers - full-stack, backend, frontend, AI/ML Founders & aspiring founders who like shipping fast Recent grads, master's students, & NYC college builders TA ops & recruiting-systems practitioners who want to build alongside engineers HR / recruiting professionals newer to the space - join a team as a product advisor You do not need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete - that's the whole point of one focused theme. Engineers go straight at the detection, identity, & verification problems; practitioners keep it real. Just show up ready to build. Credit Sponsors Solari is the world's fastest agent infrastructure provider. Run headless browsers, sandboxes, & desktops from one API, & automate at scale. Block Convey is an AI reliability & observability platform for AI agents. It helps teams see what an agent is doing across model calls, tools, retrieval & decisions, identify where it fails, & improve it. Hosts Somya Gupta: The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Integral Recruiting (IRD): Enterprise talent-acquisition & iCIMS/ATS specialists, & stewards of the ~350-member SAI community of TA operators & system admins. Greg Mendez: NYU. Bringing the university's builder & HR-analytics community into the room. TechSHRM is NYU Tandon's, award-winning student chapter of the Society for Human Resource Management (SHRM). Established in 1987, we bridge data science, technology, & organizational strategy through people analytics - leveraging data to optimize workforce decision-making, recruitment, & employee performance.

gary_2026_09_22_powering_the_ai_build_ou.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_22_powering_the_ai_build_ou.summary: Gary's Guide: CleanMax invites you to a moderated panel bringing together hyperscalers, independent power producers & other market participants to examine how India's rapidly scaling data-centre sector will meet its power demand-and what role renewable energy, storage & firm-power structures need to play in getting there. What the panel will explore The scale & geography of India's data-centre power demand-and what a realistic, bankable renewable-energy pipeline could look like through 2030. Whether renewables & storage can deliver 24/7, high-reliability power at a viable cost, & where grid, transmission, land & infrastructure constraints could limit new capacity. How hyperscalers & power producers are structuring supply-from physical & group-captive arrangements to VPPAs & CFDs-and which models are becoming genuinely bankable. The broader policy & regulatory clarity needed to accelerate investment & give developers, buyers & financiers confidence in long-term delivery. How data-centre growth can earn community acceptance & support sustainable development through transparent engagement & meaningful local benefits around land, water, infrastructure & livelihoods. Warm regards, CleanMax Team

gary_2026_09_22_tech_x_market_decoders.summary: Gary's Guide: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 6 pm - check-in. We kick off at 6.15 pm. 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Drone delivery gets regulatory approval - Now what? DoorDash just became only the eighth company ever to earn FAA air-carrier certification for drones, joining Amazon, Walmart, & Alphabet's Wing in a race that's now more about economics than regulation. We're decoding whether drone delivery can actually scale profitably or whether the real bottleneck was never the FAA to begin with. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

gary_2026_09_23_visualizing_climate_worl.title: Visualizing Climate Worlds - Data, AI & Immersive Futures
gary_2026_09_23_visualizing_climate_worl.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_23_visualizing_climate_worl.summary: Gary's Guide: Thanks to a proliferation of climate data, processed & interpreted with AI tools & new visualization methods, we can recognize new patterns in our relationship with our cities & our planet, predict extreme events or future hazards, & inform the hard work of climate adaptation & mitigation. Visualizing Climate Worlds brings together three projects that turn data into new ways of seeing - & living in - a changing planet. The Better Planet Laboratory at CU Boulder uses satellite data, sensors, & AI to monitor global food & environmental systems, transforming planetary-scale information into early-warning & decision tools for a more resilient, equitable future. MIT's Urban Metabolism Environmental Research & Action Lab (UMERA) applies Material Flow Analysis & machine learning to 11,000+ cities worldwide, surfacing productive & sometimes unexpected climate sister-city networks & modeling how they converge on unique sustainability paths to 2050. And BEAM Studio's TIDELANDS 2100 draws on NOAA flood models & the oral histories of Rhode Island's coastal residents to build immersive VR worlds of adaptation in place. Together they move from planetary monitoring to urban comparison to lived experience, asking: once we can model & see a changing planet, how do we choose to live in it? More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

gary_2026_09_23_ai_needs_more_power_who_.summary: Gary's Guide: New York's decision to temporarily halt permitting for new hyperscale data centers is the latest sign of a much bigger collision: AI needs enormous amounts of power, but who will build it, what needs to be deployed, who will finance it, & who will ultimately pay for it? From Texas & Virginia to Europe, the race to power AI is driving demand for new generation, transmission, storage & other infrastructure, & creating a potentially massive new opportunity for investors, developers & energy companies. On-site resources are becoming critical & can potentially offer flexibility while reducing ratepayer impact. Moderated by Lisa Martine Jenkins of Latitude Media, energy leaders & investors from Aston Power, Commonwealth Station A, & Redwood Materials will debate where capital is moving, what actually needs to get built, & whether the AI boom will fundamentally reshape how, & from whom, large energy users get their power Moderator: Lisa Martine Jenkins | Editor | Latitude Media Panelists: Doug Chambers | Chief Development Officer | Aston Travis Metcalfe | Energy Strategist | Commonwealth Asset Management Group Kevin Berekemeyer | Co-Founder & CEO | Station A Claire McConnell | Vice President of Business Development | Redwood Materials Antenna Group is the public relations & strategic marketing agency of choice for climate, energy, mobility, real estate, & infrastructure leaders. jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.place: ART HOUSE, 345 MARIN BLVD, JERSEY CITY
jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.summary: Experience the groundbreaking Tony Award-winning musical and Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that defined a generation. Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City’s East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them. Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship. This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions’ 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.
